name: GoConsent™ – Cookie Consent Banner & Privacy Tools
author: RoxxiStudios

sections.description:
GoConsent — cookie consent and privacy compliance tools for WordPress, for visitors anywhere in the world. The banner, tracker blocking, policies, laws and scans in one plugin: opt-in for visitors from the EU, UK, Quebec and Brazil, the opt-out rules each US state expects, 40+ privacy laws in 20+ countries in plain English, and checks for 13 kinds of business.

Privacy laws now reach small businesses everywhere. The GDPR, UK GDPR, Quebec’s Law 25 and Brazil’s LGPD expect consent before analytics and advertising cookies, and Canada, Switzerland, Australia, Japan and others set their own notice rules. California, Colorado, Texas, Virginia, Oregon and more than a dozen other US states require clear choices, an opt-out for targeted advertising, a respected Global Privacy Control signal and an up-to-date privacy policy. Lawsuits over tracking pixels and chat tools are growing every year. GoConsent works out where each visitor is, shows the banner their law expects in their own language, sets up the technical pieces from one screen and tells you in plain English what is left to fix.

Free means free. No visit limits, no account, no cloud service and no forced branding. Everything runs on your own WordPress server, so nothing about your visitors leaves your site.

At a glance

  1. Worldwide privacy laws: opt-in for visitors from the EU, UK, Quebec and Brazil (GDPR, UK GDPR, Law 25, LGPD), the opt-out rules of California (CCPA/CPRA) and the other US state laws, and Switzerland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, India, South Africa, Singapore, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, Türkiye, Israel and China, with laws that start soon flagged early.
  2. Visitor location detection: the country your CDN or host adds to each request, else GoConsent’s built-in country database on your own server, else the browser’s time zone. No IP address is stored or sent anywhere.
  3. Real tracker blocking with Google Consent Mode v2, Global Privacy Control (GPC) and the IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP).
  4. 450+ services recognised: Google Analytics, Google Ads, Meta Pixel, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, HubSpot, Klaviyo, Intercom, Calendly, Stripe and hundreds more, each with its company, purpose and cookies, plus popular plugins such as WooCommerce, Site Kit, MonsterInsights and PixelYourSite set up automatically.
  5. Embed and widget protection: maps, videos and other companies’ booking calendars, chat, reviews and forms that carry trackers wait behind a click-to-load placeholder until the visitor agrees.
  6. Free consent self-check: a clean, real browser tests your banner four ways (before any choice, after Reject All, after Accept All and with GPC on) and gives a plain-English “How to fix” for each problem.
  7. 13 business types: Health, Kids, Real estate, Restaurant, Finance, Online store, Home services, Automotive, Legal, Education, Nonprofit, Hospitality & travel, and Dating & adult.
  8. 10 languages, with an option to show the banner in each visitor’s browser language.
  9. In GoConsent Pro, Evidence Scan: the same four-visit test saved as evidence, with a PDF report, screenshots, HAR recordings and a private share link for your lawyer.
  10. Banner tested against WCAG 2.2 AA (keyboard, screen reader semantics, 400% zoom, high contrast): automated axe-core checks and scripted keyboard tests on every release, in all bundled languages. See the accessibility conformance report.

Who GoConsent is for

  • Small businesses that want the privacy basics done right without a monthly bill: shops, contractors, salons, professional services.
  • Sites with visitors from many countries: EU, UK and US visitors each get the banner their law expects, in their own language.
  • Agencies and web designers who manage many client sites and need one setup that works everywhere, including multisite networks.
  • Real estate agents and brokers: listing maps and video tours keep working, with a check that your policy covers them.
  • Restaurants: reservation and online ordering widgets (OpenTable, Resy, Tock, SevenRooms, Toast) keep working, with policy wording for reservations and allergies.
  • Health, kids and finance sites: extra checks for sensitive, children’s and financial information.
  • Online stores, contractors, auto dealers, law firms, schools, hotels and dating sites: checks and policy wording for each, from 13 business types (see below).
  • Nonprofits, churches and publishers that want consent, policies and traffic stats without sending visitor data to another company. Donation forms keep working, and only the state laws that cover nonprofits are checked.

How it works

  1. Install and accept the terms. Nothing runs and nothing leaves your site until you do.
  2. Tell GoConsent about your business: where you are, your business type and where your customers live. It works out which privacy laws likely apply to you.
  3. Scan. GoConsent reads your own pages (and your Google Tag Manager container) and lists every tracker, pixel, embed and cookie, and what adds each one.
  4. Fix. The Overview shows a score and plain-English issues, sorted by what the law requires and what is best practice. Most fixes take one click.
  5. Publish your policies. Build your Privacy Policy, Cookie Policy, Refund & Returns Policy and Accessibility Statement in your own editor, then keep them current as your site changes.

Business types

Pick one or more in Settings. Each adds plain-English checks, suggested privacy policy wording and sensible defaults for that kind of business:

  1. Health: sensitive and consumer health data, including Washington’s and Nevada’s health data policy.
  2. Kids: children’s data and COPPA.
  3. Real estate: listing maps and video tours load by default, and your policy covers them.
  4. Restaurant: reservation and ordering widgets (OpenTable, Resy, Tock, SevenRooms, Toast) always work; reservations, allergies, loyalty programs and texts are covered.
  5. Finance: financial information and GLBA.
  6. Online store: a published refund policy, payment and shipping companies, cart reminders and texts, sign-up discounts (California’s financial incentive notice) and subscription terms. Known session recorders never load on checkout, cart and account pages.
  7. Home services: contractors, roofing, HVAC, plumbing, cleaning and landscaping. Call tracking and recording, texts to quote-form leads, passing leads to partners, and review tools.
  8. Automotive: driver’s licenses, financing (GLBA and the FTC Safeguards Rule), vehicle location data, and booking, scheduling and chat tools.
  9. Legal: a “not legal advice” notice for contact forms, attorney advertising notices, and chat and intake tools.
  10. Education: FERPA, COPPA, K-12 student data (California’s SOPIPA) and lesson videos.
  11. Nonprofit: donation platforms, donor lists and religious information. Donation forms (Donorbox, Givebutter, Zeffy) always work, and only state laws that cover nonprofits are checked.
  12. Hospitality & travel: booking engines (Cloudbeds, SiteMinder, Mews, SynXis, FareHarbor, Peek, Checkfront, Rezdy, Bókun, Lodgify) always work and maps load by default; guest ID and passport details and loyalty programs are covered.
  13. Dating & adult: sexual orientation and sex life as sensitive data, sexual health data, adults-only and age verification notices, and ad pixels.

What visitors see

  • A compact banner with equal Accept All and Reject All buttons, category switches, and links to your Privacy Policy, Notice at Collection and Cookie Policy.
  • Your Privacy Choices, a dialog with a short notice at collection, one collapsible section per category with its cookies, a consent receipt they can copy, and “Opt out using your email.”
  • A “Your Privacy Choices” link with California’s opt-out icon in your footer, and a small privacy button that reopens their choices on any page.
  • Click-to-load placeholders for maps and videos, so nothing contacts Google or YouTube until they agree, and for booking, chat, review and form widgets that carry trackers.
  • The banner and Your Privacy Choices in their own language when you turn on Visitor’s browser language (10 languages).

What you see

  • Overview: checkup score, issues and one-click fixes, plus a one-time question when a better default is available.
  • Consent: every banner and privacy setting, saved instantly.
  • Requests: Do Not Sell or Share requests with due dates and a checklist.
  • Scanner: every tracker and cookie, its category and what adds it, plus a consent self-check that tests your banner in a real browser.
  • Tools: your policy pages, built and updated in your editor.
  • Laws: the privacy laws that likely apply to you, in plain English, including laws starting soon.
  • Traffic: cookie-free visitor stats on your own server.

Cookie consent banner that blocks trackers before consent

  • Equal Accept All and Reject All buttons, with category switches right on a compact banner that links to your Privacy Policy, Notice at Collection and Cookie Policy.
  • “Your Privacy Choices” panel with a short notice at collection, one collapsible section per category (analytics, advertising, maps and videos) and the cookies in each, plus California’s official opt-out icon on the “Your Privacy Choices” footer link.
  • Full cookie declaration. Every cookie and tracker the scan finds, with provider, purpose, type and expiry, listed by category for visitors and on your Cookie Policy page ([goconsent_cookie_table]).
  • Consent receipt and privacy button. Visitors see their Consent ID and can reopen their choices from a floating GoConsent shield on any page.
  • Real blocking, not just a notice. Google Analytics, Google Ads, Meta Pixel, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar and other tags wait until the visitor agrees. Scripts that other plugins add later are held too.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 with every signal set to “denied” until consent, ad data redaction on, and Google Signals and ad personalization off until a visitor allows marketing. Meta Pixel gets the same consent signal.
  • Global Privacy Control (GPC) honored automatically, as California, Colorado and other states require. Visitors are told the signal was honored, and a signed-in visitor’s GPC opt-out follows them to every device.
  • “Opt out using your email.” Visitors can ask you to stop selling or sharing information you hold about them outside the browser, with no account or ID. You get an email, a 15-business-day countdown, a step-by-step checklist and a reminder before the deadline.
  • IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP). Ad vendors that read __gpp get a US National signal that matches the visitor’s choice and GPC.
  • Analytics from the first page, privately. For US visitors, Google Analytics counts visits without cookies until they choose (you can turn this off). EU and UK visitors get stricter defaults automatically.
  • Knows where each visitor is, on every host. EU and UK visitors get opt-in, US visitors get US rules. GoConsent uses the country your CDN or host already adds to each request (Cloudflare, Amazon CloudFront, Vercel, Pantheon, Akamai, WP Engine, Kinsta and other GeoIP hosts). On hosts that add none, its built-in country database finds the country on your own server: no outside service, and the IP address is never stored or sent anywhere. Travellers and VPN users get the right banner. If neither can tell, the visitor’s time zone is used. Works with page caching.
  • Click-to-load Google Maps, Street View, YouTube and Vimeo, so a first visit makes no calls to Google.
  • Embed and widget protection. When a scan or self-check finds a tracker inside another company’s embed (a booking calendar, chat, reviews or a form), set the embed to Analytics or Marketing and visitors see a click-to-load placeholder until they agree. Booking and donation widgets your business type relies on keep working.
  • Banner in your visitor’s language. 10 languages are built in. By default the banner, Your Privacy Choices and the cookie list show in each visitor’s browser language; you can keep them in your site’s language instead (Consent tab). Pages stay cacheable, and consent works the same in every language.
  • Optional self-hosted Google Fonts. Turn it on and fonts are copied to your server, so visitors never contact Google.
  • Fast and cache-friendly. Works with page caching and loads a small script.

Cookie scanner and compliance report

  • Daily cookie and tracker scan of your own pages finds tracking tags, pixels, embeds and unknown scripts, and shows which plugin, theme or page adds each one. It recognises 450+ services (see Integrations below) and names the company behind each, what it does and the cookies it sets.
  • Plugins handled automatically. WooCommerce, Site Kit, MonsterInsights, PixelYourSite, Jetpack, HubSpot, Klaviyo, OptinMonster, the big form plugins and page builders are recognised and set up with nothing to configure; another consent plugin is flagged.
  • Sees inside Google Tag Manager. Tags hidden inside your GTM container are listed too, so your cookie list and policies stay complete.
  • Checkup score with plain-English issues, sorted by what the law requires for your business and what is only best practice.
  • One-click fixes, plus suggested privacy policy wording you can copy or add to your policy.
  • Consent self-check. With one click, a clean browser visits your site four times: before any choice, after Reject All, after Accept All, and with Global Privacy Control on. You see which trackers loaded when they shouldn’t have, including trackers hidden inside other companies’ embeds (for example a session recorder inside a booking widget), and a plain-English “How to fix” for each one with a button that takes you to the right row in the Scanner. Results show on your screen only and aren’t saved as a report. Up to 3 checks per site per day.
  • Email alerts when a new critical issue appears.

Integrations: 450+ services recognised

The scanner, the tracker blocker, the cookie list and the consent self-check all use one catalogue of 453 services: for each one the company behind it, what it does, its script and embed hosts, the cookies it sets (name, purpose and how long it lasts), whether it reads Google Consent Mode, and whether Global Privacy Control applies. Advertising is checked first, so a tag that mixes analytics and ads is held as advertising. Scripts from companies not in the catalogue are still sorted by what their address looks like, and you can change any category on the Scanner tab.

  1. Analytics, tag managers and data pipelines (45): Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, Google tag (gtag.js), Yandex Metrica, Mixpanel, Heap, Segment, Amplitude, Plausible Analytics, Matomo Cloud, StatCounter, comScore, Matomo (self-hosted), Piwik PRO, Fathom Analytics, Simple Analytics, Cloudflare Web Analytics, Umami Analytics, Ahrefs Web Analytics, Jetpack Stats, WooCommerce Analytics, WooCommerce order attribution (Sourcebuster), Adobe Analytics, Adobe Experience Platform Tags (Launch), Baidu Tongji, Naver Analytics, PostHog, Kissmetrics, Woopra, Clicky, Chartbeat, Parse.ly, Nielsen Digital Content Ratings, Gemius Audience, Pendo, Azure Application Insights, New Relic Browser, Datadog Real User Monitoring, Dynatrace, Tealium iQ, Cloudflare Zaraz, Stape (server-side tagging), Snowplow, RudderStack, mParticle.
  2. Session recording and heatmaps (11): Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, FullStory session recording, Mouseflow session recording, Lucky Orange session recording, Smartlook session recording, LogRocket session recording, Crazy Egg heatmaps, Inspectlet session recording, Contentsquare, Quantum Metric.
  3. A/B testing, personalisation and surveys (16): Adobe Target, VWO, Optimizely, AB Tasty, Convert Experiences, Kameleoon, Google Optimize (retired), Qualaroo, SurveyMonkey, Usabilla, Mopinion, Zoho PageSense, Insider personalisation, Dynamic Yield, Mutiny, Salesforce Marketing Cloud.
  4. Advertising pixels and ad tech (79): Google Ads, Google AdSense, Ad Manager and Campaign Manager 360 (DoubleClick, Floodlight), Meta (Facebook) Pixel, TikTok Pixel, LinkedIn …
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for GoConsent and click Install Now, then Activate.
  2. Open GoConsent in the admin menu and accept the terms to turn on protection.
  3. In Settings, set your business location, business type and where your customers are. GoConsent then checks your site against the laws that likely apply to you.
  4. Click Scan now on the Overview, fix what the report shows, and create your policy pages in Tools.
sections.faq:
Does GoConsent help with CCPA and CPRA?

GoConsent gives you tools for key California requirements: an opt-out for the sale and sharing of personal information, Global Privacy Control support, a “Your Privacy Choices” link with the state’s official opt-out icon, and a privacy policy that covers your rights. Compliance also depends on how your business handles data, so have a lawyer review your setup.

Does it work for GDPR and the UK?

It’s built for it. Visitors choose before any analytics or advertising cookies load, and the Privacy Policy includes a legal basis section, rights, response times and the regulator when you serve the EU or UK. For the UK you can turn on the Data (Use and Access) Act exception, which lets statistics-only analytics run with a free way to object.

Which privacy laws does GoConsent cover?

US state privacy laws (California’s CCPA/CPRA and 19 others, plus laws starting soon), CalOPPA, COPPA, GLBA and US health data laws, and outside the US: the EU GDPR and ePrivacy rules, UK GDPR and PECR, Switzerland’s FADP, Canada’s PIPEDA, Quebec’s Law 25, Brazil’s LGPD, Australia’s Privacy Act, New Zealand’s Privacy Act, Japan’s APPI, South Korea’s PIPA, India’s DPDP Act (coming 2027), South Africa’s POPIA, Singapore’s PDPA, Mexico’s LFPDPPP, Argentina’s Law 25,326, Colombia’s Law 1581, Chile’s Law 21.719 (coming Dec 1, 2026), Türkiye’s KVKK, Israel’s Protection of Privacy Law and China’s PIPL. The laws that apply to you depend on the countries and states you choose under Who you serve. Each one adds its checks to the report and its rights, deadlines and regulator to your generated Privacy Policy. GoConsent is a tool, not legal advice.

Which visitors get opt-in (nothing tracks until they agree)?

With Stricter defaults for opt-in regions on (the default): visitors from the EU and EEA, the UK, Quebec and Brazil, plus China and Argentina when you serve them. Canadian visitors whose province isn’t known count as Quebec when you serve Quebec. Swiss visitors always see the banner with a Reject option. US visitors get the opt-out rules their states expect. In GoConsent Pro you can set your own rule for each region.

Can the banner show in my visitor’s language?

Yes, by default (Banner language: Visitor’s browser language, on the Consent tab). The banner, Your Privacy Choices and the cookie dialog then show in the visitor’s browser language when it is one of GoConsent’s 10 (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Swedish and Japanese, with regional versions for Spain and Mexico, France and Canada, and Brazil and Portugal). Other visitors see your site language. The page itself stays the same for everyone, so page caching keeps working: the browser loads a small translation file from your own site only when it needs one. Trackers stay held while it loads, and consent records are the same in every language. Policy pages stay in your site language. If you use WPML, Polylang or TranslatePress, the banner follows each page’s language instead.

Does it really block Google Analytics and the Meta Pixel before consent?

Yes. Tracking tags are held until the visitor agrees, including tags added later by other scripts. Google Consent Mode v2 is set to “denied” by default.

How does GoConsent know where a visitor is?

In this order, and only the country (plus the US state or Canadian province when a header gives it):

  1. The country your CDN or host already adds to each request: Cloudflare (turn on IP Geolocation under Network in Cloudflare), Amazon CloudFront, Vercel, Pantheon, Akamai, WP Engine, Kinsta and other hosts with GeoIP.
  2. If there’s no header, GoConsent’s built-in country database. It ships inside the plugin, so it works on every host. The visitor’s IP address is checked against it on your own server, then forgotten: it is never stored, logged or sent anywhere, and no outside service is called.
  3. If neither can tell (a private network, say), or the answer takes longer than 0.8 seconds, the browser’s time zone.

Pages stay cacheable: the banner asks your own site with a tiny request that is never cached. Trackers stay held until the answer is in, so nothing loads early. Proxy headers such as X-Forwarded-For are only believed from Cloudflare or a proxy on your own network, so a visitor can’t fake a country. The database gives the country, not the US state, so without a state header US visitors get your US rules (one set for every state) and Global Privacy Control is honored everywhere. See what your server uses on the Consent tab under Visitor location, with the Check button. Developers can supply their own country with the goconsent_visitor_country filter.

Which services and plugins does GoConsent recognise?

450+ services, from Google Analytics, Google Ads, Meta Pixel, TikTok and LinkedIn to Matomo, Plausible, Hotjar, HubSpot, Klaviyo, Intercom, Calendly, Stripe, booking engines, IDX feeds and other consent tools. See “Integrations” above for the full list by group. Popular plugins such as WooCommerce, Elementor, Site Kit, MonsterInsights, PixelYourSite, Jetpack and OptinMonster are set up automatically. Scripts from other companies are still found and sorted by what their address looks like, and you can change any category.

Does it work with Elementor, Beaver Builder and page caching?

Yes. The banner works with any theme and with page caching. Policy pages can be created and updated in the block editor, the classic editor, Elementor and Beaver Builder.

Does GoConsent use cookies?

One first-party cookie, goconsent, remembers each visitor’s choice for 12 months. Traffic statistics use no cookies. When your host provides the visitor’s country, the banner also keeps it in the browser’s session storage (goconsent_where, deleted when the browser closes) so it doesn’t ask again on every page.

Will visitors who click Reject still be counted?

Yes, in GoConsent’s cookie-free traffic stats. They are not tracked by Google Analytics or advertising tools.

Can I let Google Analytics run before consent?

Yes, by default. “Analytics before consent” (Consent tab) is on for new installs: Google Analytics counts visits from the first page, without cookies until the visitor chooses. Advertising stays blocked, visitors can still opt out, and EU & UK visitors keep analytics off until they choose. Turn it off in the Consent tab.

How do I add the “Your Privacy Choices” link somewhere else?

Use the [goconsent_choices] shortcode, or link any menu item to #privacy-choices. The floating privacy button (Consent › Banner look) can sit bottom left or bottom right, at any height, or be turned off.

How do I show the list of cookies on a page?

Use the [goconsent_cookie_table] shortcode. Add category="analytics" (or necessary, media, marketing) to show one category. The Cookie Policy page GoConsent builds already includes it.

Are there visit limits or a paid plan required?

No. The free version has no visit or page limits, needs no account and adds no forced branding. Everything runs on your own server, except the consent self-check, which uses the GoConsent server only when you click Run self-check.

Does it support IAB GPP and TCF?

GoConsent sends an IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP) US National signal that matches each visitor’s choice and Global Privacy Control. IAB TCF (needed only for sites that serve personalized Google ads to European visitors) is not included.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. Shop managers count as staff, so the banner never gets in their way. Checkout and payment scripts (Stripe, PayPal) are treated as necessary. GoConsent also sets the WP Consent API, which WooCommerce and other plugins read to respect each visitor’s choice.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The banner and choices run in the visitor’s browser, so cached pages work. When GoConsent changes how pages load, it asks Hummingbird, LiteSpeed Cache, Breeze, SiteGround Optimizer, WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache and WP Super Cache to clear their caches.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Network activation sets up every site. Each site accepts the terms, chooses its settings and keeps its own consent and request records.

Is the banner accessible?

It is tested against WCAG 2.2 AA on every release. Automated axe-core checks run inside the banner across three banner positions, phone and desktop widths, 200% and 400% zoom, light and dark pages, extreme button colors, right-to-left text, Windows high contrast, reduced motion and all 13 bundled languages, with 0 violations. Scripted keyboard tests cover Tab and Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and Escape, focus moving into and back out of dialogs, visible focus, page focus never hidden behind the open banner, and announced status messages. The accessibility conformance report lists every WCAG 2.2 AA criterion as Supports, Partially supports or Not applicable, with notes. It is a self-assessment; an independent audit is planned. Your theme and page content are outside what GoConsent can test.

Will my team see the banner?

No. Administrators and editors never see it, so page builders and admin tools work normally. Authors, contributors and CRM roles skip it too unless you untick them. Use Preview on the Consent tab to see the banner as visitors do.

What happens when I delete GoConsent?

Deleting the plugin removes its settings, scans, reports, consent and request records, traffic stats and stored fonts from every site where it ran. Deactivating keeps everything, in case you turn it back on. If GoConsent Pro is also installed, the shared data is kept for it.

What is the consent self-check?

A test of your banner in a real browser, from outside your site. Click Run self-check on the Scanner tab: a clean browser visits your site four times (before any choice, after Reject All, after Accept All, and with Global Privacy Control on) and reports which trackers loaded when they shouldn’t have. For each problem you get a short “How to fix”, such as “Set Hotjar to Analytics in Scanner”. A check takes about 4 to 5 minutes; you can leave the page and come back. It’s free, up to 3 checks per site per day.

Is the self-check saved or shared anywhere?

No. The result shows on your own admin screen only. GoConsent keeps just the latest result on your site, for you. The GoConsent server deletes the scanner’s recordings, screenshots and report as they arrive, makes no share link and deletes its record once your site has the result. If you need proof you can keep or send to a lawyer (a PDF report, raw recordings and a share link), that’s GoConsent Pro’s evidence scan.

What is a HAR file and why does it matter?

A HAR (HTTP Archive) file is a browser’s own record of every request it made while loading pages: each address, response status, redirect, header, cookie and timing. GoConsent Pro’s evidence scan saves one for each of its four visits, made by GoConsent’s own clean test browser, so there is no visitor data in them, and page contents aren’t saved. They show exactly which trackers loaded before and after a choice, with timestamps, which is the kind of technical record experts and lawyers look at when a demand letter claims a site tracked people without consent. The PDF report lists a SHA-256 fingerprint for each file so anyone can check it wasn’t changed. The free self-check keeps no HAR files. It’s not legal advice. See HAR files: your evidence, explained.

Can someone else run a self-check on my site?

No. Only an administrator signed in to your site can start one. The GoConsent server checks with your site that the request came from your own admin before it starts.

Does GoConsent send my data anywhere?

No visitor data ever leaves your site. Scans, reports, consent records and traffic stats stay in your own WordPress database. Only when you click Run self-check does GoConsent send your site’s address, page addresses and its tracker list to the GoConsent server. See External services below.

After 14 days of protection, GoConsent’s own screen may ask once for a review on WordPress.org. Nothing is sent anywhere: the button just opens WordPress.org in a new tab, and your answer is saved on your own site.
sections.changelog:
1.0.117

  • A one-time, easy-to-dismiss review request after 14 days of protection, shown only on GoConsent’s own screen.

1.0.116

  • Readme: explains HAR files.

1.0.115

  • Accessibility: full WCAG 2.2 AA audit of everything visitors see, with fixes in both the free and Pro builds. New public accessibility conformance report.
  • The open banner now comes first in the keyboard and screen reader order (it stays where it is on screen), and never traps focus.
  • After Accept All, Reject All or Save, “Your privacy choices have been saved.” is announced to screen readers and focus moves to the privacy button instead of the top of the page. “Copied” is announced too.
  • Dialogs: marked modal and described; each category’s toggle is now a heading, so screen reader users can jump between categories; focus returns to whatever opened the dialog, or the privacy button.
  • 400% zoom and short screens: the banner scrolls inside itself and never covers more than three quarters of the screen; the dialog header stops sticking on short screens. Long German, Dutch and French button labels wrap instead of being cut off, also with text spacing increased.
  • Colors: mid-tone button colors such as #777777 now get black text (4.5:1 or more), and the age gate uses the same contrast-checked colors as the banner. Windows high contrast: switches show their on/off state, and the banner, dialogs and privacy button keep their outlines.
  • Focus: a white ring keeps the privacy button’s focus visible on dark pages; click-to-load cards get a white focus ring; footer and legal links use the page’s own text color. Page links you tab to stay clear of the open banner, right to the end of the page.
  • Click-to-load maps, videos and booking widgets: each placeholder is a named group, its button is described by the notice, the loaded frame gets a title, and focus moves into it after loading. The placeholder takes the banner’s language.
  • Footer “Your Privacy Choices” link answers the Space key, and footer, legal and banner links have 24px targets.
  • Age gate (Pro): the page behind it is inert for keyboard and screen reader users, and date-of-birth errors are flagged on the fields.
  • Policy pages and the proof-of-consent receipt: table headers are marked as column headers.
  • Admin: toasts are announced once, errors stay until closed, and the tabs work with the arrow keys.
  • New text is translated into the 10 included languages.

1.0.114

  • New: global privacy laws. GoConsent now covers 20 laws outside the US: EU GDPR and ePrivacy, UK GDPR and PECR, Switzerland (FADP), Canada (PIPEDA), Quebec (Law 25), Brazil (LGPD), Australia, New Zealand, Japan (APPI), South Korea (PIPA), India (DPDP, from 2027), South Africa (POPIA), Singapore (PDPA), Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, Chile (from Dec 1, 2026), Türkiye (KVKK), Israel and China (PIPL). Each has a Laws tab card with who it covers, its cookie rule, response deadlines and regulator.
  • New: “Where your customers are” lists 20 countries and regions in four groups and saves as you click. Until you choose, GoConsent suggests them from your site language and WooCommerce store.
  • New: opt-in visitors. “Stricter defaults for opt-in regions” (was “for EU & UK visitors”) now also covers Quebec and Brazil, plus China and Argentina when you serve them. Canadian visitors whose province isn’t known get Quebec’s rules when you serve Quebec. Switzerland always gets the banner with Reject.
  • New: UK analytics without consent (off by default). Since Feb 5, 2026, UK law lets statistics-only analytics run if visitors are told and can object for free; advertising and maps & videos still wait.
  • New: your generated Privacy Policy adds “Your rights by country and region” (rights, response times and a link to each regulator), Quebec’s person in charge, Brazil’s encarregado, your EU and UK representatives and transfers to other countries. short_description: Cookie consent banner for GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA, US state laws and 18 more privacy laws worldwide, with real tracker blocking, Consent Mode v2 and GPC.
description:
GoConsent — cookie consent and privacy compliance tools for WordPress, for visitors anywhere in the world. The banner, tracker blocking, policies, laws and scans in one plugin: opt-in for visitors from the EU, UK, Quebec and Brazil, the opt-out rules each US state expects, 40+ privacy laws in 20+ countries in plain English, and checks for 13 kinds of business.

Privacy laws now reach small businesses everywhere. The GDPR, UK GDPR, Quebec’s Law 25 and Brazil’s LGPD expect consent before analytics and advertising cookies, and Canada, Switzerland, Australia, Japan and others set their own notice rules. California, Colorado, Texas, Virginia, Oregon and more than a dozen other US states require clear choices, an opt-out for targeted advertising, a respected Global Privacy Control signal and an up-to-date privacy policy. Lawsuits over tracking pixels and chat tools are growing every year. GoConsent works out where each visitor is, shows the banner their law expects in their own language, sets up the technical pieces from one screen and tells you in plain English what is left to fix.

Free means free. No visit limits, no account, no cloud service and no forced branding. Everything runs on your own WordPress server, so nothing about your visitors leaves your site.

At a glance

  1. Worldwide privacy laws: opt-in for visitors from the EU, UK, Quebec and Brazil (GDPR, UK GDPR, Law 25, LGPD), the opt-out rules of California (CCPA/CPRA) and the other US state laws, and Switzerland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, India, South Africa, Singapore, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, Türkiye, Israel and China, with laws that start soon flagged early.
  2. Visitor location detection: the country your CDN or host adds to each request, else GoConsent’s built-in country database on your own server, else the browser’s time zone. No IP address is stored or sent anywhere.
  3. Real tracker blocking with Google Consent Mode v2, Global Privacy Control (GPC) and the IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP).
  4. 450+ services recognised: Google Analytics, Google Ads, Meta Pixel, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, HubSpot, Klaviyo, Intercom, Calendly, Stripe and hundreds more, each with its company, purpose and cookies, plus popular plugins such as WooCommerce, Site Kit, MonsterInsights and PixelYourSite set up automatically.
  5. Embed and widget protection: maps, videos and other companies’ booking calendars, chat, reviews and forms that carry trackers wait behind a click-to-load placeholder until the visitor agrees.
  6. Free consent self-check: a clean, real browser tests your banner four ways (before any choice, after Reject All, after Accept All and with GPC on) and gives a plain-English “How to fix” for each problem.
  7. 13 business types: Health, Kids, Real estate, Restaurant, Finance, Online store, Home services, Automotive, Legal, Education, Nonprofit, Hospitality & travel, and Dating & adult.
  8. 10 languages, with an option to show the banner in each visitor’s browser language.
  9. In GoConsent Pro, Evidence Scan: the same four-visit test saved as evidence, with a PDF report, screenshots, HAR recordings and a private share link for your lawyer.
  10. Banner tested against WCAG 2.2 AA (keyboard, screen reader semantics, 400% zoom, high contrast): automated axe-core checks and scripted keyboard tests on every release, in all bundled languages. See the accessibility conformance report.

Who GoConsent is for

  • Small businesses that want the privacy basics done right without a monthly bill: shops, contractors, salons, professional services.
  • Sites with visitors from many countries: EU, UK and US visitors each get the banner their law expects, in their own language.
  • Agencies and web designers who manage many client sites and need one setup that works everywhere, including multisite networks.
  • Real estate agents and brokers: listing maps and video tours keep working, with a check that your policy covers them.
  • Restaurants: reservation and online ordering widgets (OpenTable, Resy, Tock, SevenRooms, Toast) keep working, with policy wording for reservations and allergies.
  • Health, kids and finance sites: extra checks for sensitive, children’s and financial information.
  • Online stores, contractors, auto dealers, law firms, schools, hotels and dating sites: checks and policy wording for each, from 13 business types (see below).
  • Nonprofits, churches and publishers that want consent, policies and traffic stats without sending visitor data to another company. Donation forms keep working, and only the state laws that cover nonprofits are checked.

How it works

  1. Install and accept the terms. Nothing runs and nothing leaves your site until you do.
  2. Tell GoConsent about your business: where you are, your business type and where your customers live. It works out which privacy laws likely apply to you.
  3. Scan. GoConsent reads your own pages (and your Google Tag Manager container) and lists every tracker, pixel, embed and cookie, and what adds each one.
  4. Fix. The Overview shows a score and plain-English issues, sorted by what the law requires and what is best practice. Most fixes take one click.
  5. Publish your policies. Build your Privacy Policy, Cookie Policy, Refund & Returns Policy and Accessibility Statement in your own editor, then keep them current as your site changes.

Business types

Pick one or more in Settings. Each adds plain-English checks, suggested privacy policy wording and sensible defaults for that kind of business:

  1. Health: sensitive and consumer health data, including Washington’s and Nevada’s health data policy.
  2. Kids: children’s data and COPPA.
  3. Real estate: listing maps and video tours load by default, and your policy covers them.
  4. Restaurant: reservation and ordering widgets (OpenTable, Resy, Tock, SevenRooms, Toast) always work; reservations, allergies, loyalty programs and texts are covered.
  5. Finance: financial information and GLBA.
  6. Online store: a published refund policy, payment and shipping companies, cart reminders and texts, sign-up discounts (California’s financial incentive notice) and subscription terms. Known session recorders never load on checkout, cart and account pages.
  7. Home services: contractors, roofing, HVAC, plumbing, cleaning and landscaping. Call tracking and recording, texts to quote-form leads, passing leads to partners, and review tools.
  8. Automotive: driver’s licenses, financing (GLBA and the FTC Safeguards Rule), vehicle location data, and booking, scheduling and chat tools.
  9. Legal: a “not legal advice” notice for contact forms, attorney advertising notices, and chat and intake tools.
  10. Education: FERPA, COPPA, K-12 student data (California’s SOPIPA) and lesson videos.
  11. Nonprofit: donation platforms, donor lists and religious information. Donation forms (Donorbox, Givebutter, Zeffy) always work, and only state laws that cover nonprofits are checked.
  12. Hospitality & travel: booking engines (Cloudbeds, SiteMinder, Mews, SynXis, FareHarbor, Peek, Checkfront, Rezdy, Bókun, Lodgify) always work and maps load by default; guest ID and passport details and loyalty programs are covered.
  13. Dating & adult: sexual orientation and sex life as sensitive data, sexual health data, adults-only and age verification notices, and ad pixels.

Cookie consent banner that blocks trackers before consent

  • Equal Accept All and Reject All buttons, with category switches right on a compact banner that links to your Privacy Policy, Notice at Collection and Cookie Policy.
  • “Your Privacy Choices” panel with a short notice at collection, one collapsible section per category (analytics, advertising, maps and videos) and the cookies in each, plus California’s official opt-out icon on the “Your Privacy Choices” footer link.
  • Full cookie declaration. Every cookie and tracker the scan finds, with provider, purpose, type and expiry, listed by category for visitors and on your Cookie Policy page ([goconsent_cookie_table]).
  • Consent receipt and privacy button. Visitors see their Consent ID and can reopen their choices from a floating GoConsent shield on any page.
  • Real blocking, not just a notice. Google Analytics, Google Ads, Meta Pixel, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar and other tags wait until the visitor agrees. Scripts that other plugins add later are held too.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 with every signal set to “denied” until consent, ad data redaction on, and Google Signals and ad personalization off until a visitor allows marketing. Meta Pixel gets the same consent signal.
  • Global Privacy Control (GPC) honored automatically, as California, Colorado and other states require. Visitors are told the signal was honored, and a signed-in visitor’s GPC opt-out follows them to every device.
  • “Opt out using your email.” Visitors can ask you to stop selling or sharing information you hold about them outside the browser, with no account or ID. You get an email, a 15-business-day countdown, a step-by-step checklist and a reminder before the deadline.
  • IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP). Ad vendors that read __gpp get a US National signal that matches the visitor’s choice and GPC.
  • Analytics from the first page, privately. For US visitors, Google Analytics counts visits without cookies until they choose (you can turn this off). EU and UK visitors get stricter defaults automatically.
  • Knows where each visitor is, on every host. EU and UK visitors get opt-in, US visitors get US rules. GoConsent uses the country your CDN or host already adds to each request (Cloudflare, Amazon CloudFront, Vercel, Pantheon, Akamai, WP Engine, Kinsta and other GeoIP hosts). On hosts that add none, its built-in country database finds the country on your own server: no outside service, and the IP address is never stored or sent anywhere. Travellers and VPN users get the right banner. If neither can tell, the visitor’s time zone is used. Works with page caching.
  • Click-to-load Google Maps, Street View, YouTube and Vimeo, so a first visit makes no calls to Google.
  • Embed and widget protection. When a scan or self-check finds a tracker inside another company’s embed (a booking calendar, chat, reviews or a form), set the embed to Analytics or Marketing and visitors see a click-to-load placeholder until they agree. Booking and donation widgets your business type relies on keep working.
  • Banner in your visitor’s language. 10 languages are built in. By default the banner, Your Privacy Choices and the cookie list show in each visitor’s browser language; you can keep them in your site’s language instead (Consent tab). Pages stay cacheable, and consent works the same in every language.
  • Optional self-hosted Google Fonts. Turn it on and fonts are copied to your server, so visitors never contact Google.
  • Fast and cache-friendly. Works with page caching and loads a small script.
